correctness.rationale: Bounded Hardy operator and finite-support difference right inverse yield a bounded Copson-plus-shift B with BC=C*. Its column Gram matrix is exactly U*DKDU; direct finite checks corroborate the algebra. The resulting self-adjoint Hilbert–Schmidt defect is a positive diagonal plus a real rank-one form and an imaginary ordered area term. Harmonic witnesses give respectively one or arbitrarily many independent negative directions. Density transfers finite negative indices through C. Compact spectral theory converts inertia into eigenvalue counts. A Hilbert–Schmidt perturbation estimate proves smallness as imaginary shift tends to zero. Full analytical proof in RESULT.md; finite checker passed 3888 tests.

value.rationale: The exact negative spectral multiplicity jumps from 0 or 1 on the real-shift line to infinitely many under arbitrarily small imaginary/Hilbert–Schmidt perturbations. This is a substantive, sharp instability of classical Cesàro hyponormality, with a complete natural complex-parameter trichotomy and a constructive explanation via four-phase harmonic blocks. Neither a routine numerical re-evaluation nor a renaming of the known real-shift criterion.
